chunks: ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, said: Some of our companions informed me, raising it to Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام was brought a man who had been found in a ruin, with a knife in his hand stained with blood, while there was a slaughtered man writhing in his blood. So Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام said to him: “What do you say?” He said: “O Amīr al-Muʾminīn, I killed him.” He said: “Take him away and execute retribution upon him.”

So when they took him away to kill him, a man came rushing and said: “Do not hasten; return him to Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام.” So they brought him back, and he said: “By Allah, O Amīr al-Muʾminīn, this man did not kill his companion; I killed him.” Then Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام said to the first man: “What led you to confess against yourself?” He said: “O Amīr al-Muʾminīn, what could I say, when men like these had testified against me, and they seized me while there was in my hand a knife stained with blood, and the man was writhing in his blood while I was standing over him? I feared beating, so I confessed. I am a man who had slaughtered a sheep beside this ruin, then I was overcome by the need to urinate, so I entered the ruin and found the man writhing in his blood. I stood there in astonishment, then these men came upon me and seized me.” So Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام said: “Take these two and go with them to al-Ḥasan عليه السلام, and say to him: What is the ruling concerning them?” He said: So they went to al-Ḥasan عليه السلام and related to him their story. Then al-Ḥasan عليه السلام said: “Say to Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام: If this one killed that man, then he has given life to this one, and Allah, the Exalted, has said:”
“And whoever gives it life, it is as though he has given life to all mankind.”
So he let them both go, and he paid the blood-money of the slain man from the public treasury.”

key_terms.أَحْيَاهَا: gave it life; cited from the Qur'anic expression about saving a life
key_terms.الْحُكْمُ: the legal judgment or ruling in the case
key_terms.خَرِبَةٍ: a ruin or desolate structure where the incident took place
key_terms.دِيَةَ: blood-money paid for the slain person
key_terms.سِكِّينٌ: a knife found in the suspect’s hand
key_terms.مُتَلَطِّخٌ: stained or smeared, here with blood

ai.seo_question: How did Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام judge a murder case involving a false confession and the real killer’s later admission?
ai.summary: This report narrates a judicial case before Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام involving a false confession made under fearful circumstances and the later appearance of the actual killer. Imam al-Ḥasan عليه السلام judged that sparing the innocent man was like giving him life, invoking the Qur'anic principle of the sanctity of life, and the diyyah was paid from Bayt al-Māl.
